library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Duwal_2019_efavirenz"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Duwal_2019_efavirenz"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2019.00199> (open access, PMC6424904)
* PK model source: Dickinson et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2015;98:406-416,
  <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.156>

Duwal et al. asked whether the cheap, patent-expired non-nucleoside reverse
transcriptase inhibitor efavirenz (EFV) could serve as HIV-1 pre-exposure
prophylaxis (PrEP). They combined three layers:

1. the ENCORE1 population PK model of oral EFV (one compartment, CYP2B6 /
   CYP2A6 genotype effects on clearance), extended with an explicit
   metabolic-autoinduction time course;
2. a sigmoid Emax inhibition of reverse transcription, parameterised from ex
   vivo IC50 and Hill coefficients for wild-type HIV-1 and three EFV-resistant
   mutants and corrected for plasma protein binding;
3. a stochastic model of the first viral replication cycles after exposure,
   from which the prophylactic efficacy (relative reduction of infection risk)
   follows.

The packaged model carries all three layers. For the third it carries the
deterministic parts: the expected-value (mean-field) ODEs of the six viral
reactions, and the closed-form efficacy against a single transmitted virion
that the current EFV concentration would give if held constant -- the
quantity of Figure 2A. The hybrid stochastic simulations behind Figures 3-4
(random exposure times, random inocula, missed doses) are a simulation
protocol on top of these equations and are not reproduced here.

# Population

The PK model was developed by Dickinson et al. on the ENCORE1 trial: 606
treatment-naive adults with HIV-1 (32% female; median age 35 years, range
18-69; median weight 65 kg, range 39-148) randomised to EFV 400 mg or 600 mg
once daily with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate / emtricitabine, at sites in
Africa, Asia, South America, Europe and Oceania. Most were of African (37%) or
Asian (33%) ethnicity, the rest Hispanic (17%), Caucasian (13%) or Aboriginal
and Torres Strait Islander (0.2%). The 1491 plasma samples were single random
samples 8-16 h post-dose at weeks 4 and 12, plus a 0-24 h profile in a
subgroup between weeks 4 and 8 (Duwal 2019 Section 2). The viral-dynamics and
PD constants come from the literature (Tables 2-3), not from ENCORE1.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Duwal_2019_efavirenz")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | Eqs. (1)-(3) | Section 3.1.1 |
| `lka` | log(0.6), fixed | Section 3.1.1 (Arab-Alameddine 2009) |
| `lcl` (CLss/F) | log(11.9) L/h | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V/F) | log(282) L | Table 1 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table 1 legend |
| Autoinduction `cl(t)` | Eq. (4) | Section 3.1.2 (Zhu 2009) |
| `cl_time_fdef` | 1 - 5.76/9.86 = 0.416 | Section 3.1.2 (alpha = 0.58, Table 1) |
| `lcl_t50` | log(245) h | Section 3.1.2 |
| `e_geno0100_cl` ... `e_geno2011_cl`, `e_genomiss_cl` | 0.18-0.96 | Supplementary Table 2 (from Dickinson 2015) |
| `etalcl` | 0.1256 (36.6% CV) | Table 1 |
| `etaiov_lcl_1..3` | 0.04315 (21.0% CV) | Table 1 |
| `propSd` | 0.20 | Table 1 |
| Direct effect `eta_d_*` | Eq. (5) | Section 3.2 |
| `lic50`, `hill` | log(5.4) nM, 1.69 | Table 2 (Shen 2008) |
| IC50 protein-binding correction | x 2 / (fu + 1) | Supplementary Text 1, Eq. (S1.10) |
| `fu` | 0.002 | Figure 2 legend, Supplementary Text 1 |
| Molar mass | 315.6 g/mol | Section 3.1 |
| `ic50_fold_*`, `hill_fold_*`, `fitness_*` | Y181C 2.8 / 0.9 / 0.78; K103N 89.1 / 0.83 / 0.74; G190S 72.1 / 0.6 / 0.24 | Table 2 (Sampah 2011) |
| `etalic50`, `etahill` | 0.0274, 0.0064 | Table 2 (sd 0.9 on 5.4; sd 0.08) |
| Viral ODEs | reactions (6)-(11) | Section 3.3 |
| `lambda_t`, `delta_t`, `delta_t1`, `delta_t2`, `delta_pic_t`, `k_t`, `beta_t`, `n_t`, `cl_virus_naive` | 2e9, 0.02, 0.02, 1, 0.35, 0.35, 8e-12, 670, 2.3 | Table 3 |
| `rho_rev` | 0.5 | Section 3.3 |
| `phi_*` | Eq. (13), single virion | Section 3.6, Figure 2A |

The prophylactic efficacy `phi` is the one place where the model goes beyond
what the paper prints: Duwal et al. cite their earlier analytical solution
rather than reprinting it. The packaged form is derived directly from the
paper's reactions (6)-(11): the extinction probability of the branching
process they define, with the drug effect held constant. The check below that
it reproduces the paper's four 90%-protective concentrations exactly is what
validates it.

# Virtual cohort

The paper's 1000 virtual patients are listed in Supplementary Table 1
(individual CLss/F and V/F). Their V/F carries no random effect, so their body
weights follow from it (`WT = 70 * V / 282`): median 66 kg, 2.5th-97.5th
percentile 42-94 kg. The cohort below draws weights from a log-normal with
that median and spread, and draws the four genotype positions independently
from the ENCORE1 allele frequencies (Dickinson 2015 Table 1), with 5.3%
missing genotype (32 of 606).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190313)

geno_cols <- c(
  "SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT", "SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT",
  "SNP_CYP2A6_RS8192726", "SNP_CYP2A6_RS28399454", "CYP2B6_MISSING"
)

draw_subjects <- function(n, id_offset = 0L) {
  out <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(66), 0.20)), 39), 148),
    SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = sample(0:2, n, TRUE, prob = c(253, 262, 59)),
    SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT = sample(0:2, n, TRUE, prob = c(535, 36, 3)),
    SNP_CYP2A6_RS8192726 = rbinom(n, 1, 104 / 570),
    SNP_CYP2A6_RS28399454 = rbinom(n, 1, 58 / 572),
    CYP2B6_MISSING = rbinom(n, 1, 32 / 606),
    OCC = 1L
  )
  # Supplementary Table 2 has no estimate for 516TT with a 983 C allele, nor
  # for 516GT / 983 C carrier / both CYP2A6 variants; the model returns NA
  # clearance there, so redraw those subjects as 516GG / 983TT (0.7% of draws).
  unlisted <- with(out, CYP2B6_MISSING == 0 &
    ((SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT == 2 & SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT >= 1) |
      (SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT == 1 & SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT >= 1 &
        SNP_CYP2A6_RS8192726 == 1 & SNP_CYP2A6_RS28399454 == 1)))
  out$SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT[unlisted] <- 0L
  out$SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT[unlisted] <- 0L
  out
}

n_arm <- 200
subjects <- bind_rows(
  draw_subjects(n_arm, 0L) |> mutate(treatment = "400 mg"),
  draw_subjects(n_arm, n_arm) |> mutate(treatment = "600 mg")
) |>
  mutate(dose = ifelse(treatment == "400 mg", 400, 600))

# Daily dosing for 30 days; observations dense over the first 4 days and on
# day 30, every 3 h in between, and just before each dose (troughs).
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 96, by = 0.25),
  seq(96, 720, by = 3),
  seq(696, 720, by = 0.25),
  24 * (1:30) - 0.01
)))

make_events <- function(subj) {
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = 24 * (0:29)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, treatment, WT, all_of(geno_cols), OCC)
}
events <- make_events(subjects)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
# rxode2 notes at parse time that the occasion-indexed IOV etas cannot be
# mu-referenced (they are multiplied by OCC indicators); that only matters for
# estimation, so this one message is muffled. The same helper muffles the
# 'multi-subject simulation without omega' note for the typical-value solves
# of zeroRe() models below, where zero variability is the point.
muffle_known <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("non-mu referenced|multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}
mod <- muffle_known(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Duwal_2019_efavirenz")))
mod_typ <- muffle_known(rxode2::zeroRe(mod))
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("treatment"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$cl))
```

# Pharmacokinetics (Figure 1)

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
fig1 <- sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    q025 = quantile(Cc, 0.025), q25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25),
    q50 = median(Cc), q75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75), q975 = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
plot_band <- function(d, xlab, tscale) {
  ggplot(d, aes(time / tscale)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975), fill = "grey85") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), fill = "grey60") +
    geom_line(aes(y = q50), colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~treatment) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "EFV plasma concentration (mg/L)")
}
plot_band(filter(fig1, time <= 96), "Time after initial dose (days)", 24) +
  labs(title = "First four days", caption = "Replicates Figure 1A-B of Duwal 2019.")
plot_band(fig1, "Time after initial dose (days)", 24) +
  labs(title = "Thirty days of daily dosing", caption = "Replicates Figure 1C-D of Duwal 2019.")
```

As in the paper, concentrations rise over the first 4-5 doses and then drift
down as autoinduction raises clearance from 58% to 100% of its steady-state
value with a 245 h half-time; the 95% band widens because slow-metaboliser
genotypes accumulate.

## Clearance and half-life against Supplementary Table 1 and the Results

The paper reports half-lives computed from the individual parameters: median
35.57 h (95% range 14.28-125.26) on day 1 and 20.77 h (8.34-73.15) after
autoinduction. The steady-state clearance distribution can also be compared
with the paper's own 1000 virtual patients (Supplementary Table 1: mean 9.86,
median 8.96, quartiles 6.07-12.39 L/h).

```{r half-life}
indiv <- sim |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  summarise(cl0 = first(cl), cl_ss = first(cl_ss), vc = first(vc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(thalf_day1 = log(2) * vc / cl0, thalf_ss = log(2) * vc / cl_ss)

hl_tab <- tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "t1/2 day 1 (h), median", "t1/2 after autoinduction (h), median",
    "CLss/F (L/h), mean", "CLss/F (L/h), median",
    "CLss/F (L/h), 25th percentile", "CLss/F (L/h), 75th percentile"
  ),
  Published = c(35.57, 20.77, 9.86, 8.96, 6.07, 12.39),
  Simulated = c(
    median(indiv$thalf_day1), median(indiv$thalf_ss),
    mean(indiv$cl_ss), median(indiv$cl_ss),
    quantile(indiv$cl_ss, 0.25), quantile(indiv$cl_ss, 0.75)
  )
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Simulated / Published - 1))
knitr::kable(hl_tab, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 1))

# The day-1 / steady-state half-life ratio is fixed by the model
# (1 / alpha), so it is checked tightly; the cohort medians are checked
# loosely because 400 simulated subjects carry ~6% sampling error on a median.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(indiv$thalf_day1 / indiv$thalf_ss) - 9.86 / 5.76) < 1e-6,
  abs(median(indiv$thalf_ss) / 20.77 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(mean(indiv$cl_ss) / 9.86 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

## PKNCA: first-dose and day-30 exposure

The paper reports a median tmax of 5.90 h (95% range 4.56-7.88) and median
trough concentrations after autoinduction of 1.35 mg/L (0.30-6.55) for
400 mg and 2.02 mg/L (0.45-9.83) for 600 mg.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 696),
  end = c(24, 720),
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# tmax is computed only on the first-dose interval and cmin only on the
# day-30 interval, so grouping by treatment alone pairs each with its value.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~tmax, ~cmin,
  "400 mg", 5.90, 1.35,
  "600 mg", 5.90, 2.02
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("tmax", "cmin"),
  units = c(tmax = "h", cmin = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated (median) vs published: first-dose Tmax and day-30 trough",
  "(published: after autoinduction). * differs by >20%."
))
```

The first-dose tmax matches, and the day-30 median troughs are within 5% of
the published values. The paper does not say at what time its "after
autoinduction" troughs were taken. At day 30, clearance has reached about 87%
of its steady-state value. With autoinduction complete, the paper's own
Supplementary Table 1 patients give a median 400 mg trough of 1.27 mg/L
(closed-form steady state, computed by the maintainers), 6% below the printed
1.35 mg/L, so the printed value must come from a finite time after the start
of therapy.

```{r trough-check}
troughs <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 719.99) < 1e-6) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(Cc), q025 = quantile(Cc, 0.025), q975 = quantile(Cc, 0.975),
    pct_ever_gt10 = NA_real_, .groups = "drop"
  )
ever10 <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment, id) |>
  summarise(ever = any(Cc > 10), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(pct_ever_gt10 = 100 * mean(ever), .groups = "drop")
troughs$pct_ever_gt10 <- ever10$pct_ever_gt10[match(troughs$treatment, ever10$treatment)]
troughs <- troughs |>
  mutate(
    published_median = c(1.35, 2.02),
    published_pct_gt10 = c(2.5, 11.3)
  )
knitr::kable(troughs, digits = 2, caption = "Day-30 trough (mg/L) and percentage of subjects ever above 10 mg/L.")

stopifnot(
  # Linear PK: the 600/400 trough ratio is 1.5 up to cohort noise.
  abs(troughs$median[2] / troughs$median[1] / 1.5 - 1) < 0.2,
  all(abs(troughs$median / troughs$published_median - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

The percentage of subjects who ever exceed 10 mg/L is shown for comparison
with the paper's 11.3% (600 mg) and 2.5% (400 mg) but is not used as a check,
because it is a known deviation. It is a tail statistic (sampling error about
2 percentage points with 200 subjects per arm), and the paper does not
reproduce it from its own cohort either: running the 1000 patients of
Supplementary Table 1 through this model gives 6.8% (600 mg) and 1.3%
(400 mg) over 30 or 120 days. The paper's simulation protocol evidently
differs in a way it does not describe, for example by adding residual error
to the simulated concentrations.

# Concentration-prophylaxis profile (Figure 2)

Figure 2A shows the prophylactic efficacy against a single transmitted virion
as a function of a constant EFV plasma concentration. The model's `phi_*`
outputs are exactly this quantity. To evaluate them at fixed concentrations,
each simulated subject receives an intravenous bolus into `central` equal to
the target concentration times V/F with clearance set to (almost) zero, so
`Cc` stays constant.

```{r figure-2-setup}
conc_grid <- 10^seq(-4, log10(25), length.out = 300)
conc_events <- function(conc, n_rep = 1L) {
  tibble(id = seq_along(rep(conc, each = n_rep)), conc = rep(conc, each = n_rep)) |>
    tidyr::crossing(evid = c(1L, 0L)) |>
    mutate(
      time = ifelse(evid == 1L, 0, 1),
      amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, conc * 282, 0),
      cmt = "central",
      WT = 70,
      SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = 0L, SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT = 0L,
      SNP_CYP2A6_RS8192726 = 0L, SNP_CYP2A6_RS28399454 = 0L,
      CYP2B6_MISSING = 0L, OCC = 1L
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
no_clearance <- c(lcl = log(1e-12))

# Typical-value curve: all random effects zero.
phi_typ <- muffle_known(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  events = conc_events(conc_grid),
  params = no_clearance,
  keep = "conc",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)) |>
  filter(time == 1)

# 90%-protective concentrations (ng/mL) by log-linear interpolation of the
# monotone curve, against the paper's Abstract and Results.
# Only the rising part of the curve is used: phi is flat at 0 and at 1 at
# the ends of the grid, and approx() needs distinct x values.
ec_at <- function(conc, phi, level) {
  rising <- phi > 0.01 & phi < 0.999
  10^approx(phi[rising], log10(conc[rising]), xout = level)$y * 1000
}
ec90 <- tibble(
  strain = c("wild type", "Y181C", "K103N", "G190S"),
  column = c("phi_wt", "phi_y181c", "phi_k103n", "phi_g190s"),
  published_ng_ml = c(11, 36, 1287, 1486)
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(simulated_ng_ml = ec_at(phi_typ$conc, phi_typ[[column]], 0.9)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (simulated_ng_ml / published_ng_ml - 1))
knitr::kable(select(ec90, -column), digits = 1,
  caption = "Plasma concentration giving 90% protection against a single virion.")

# Deterministic typical-value curve against values the paper prints as whole
# ng/mL: allow half a unit of the printed rounding (11 covers 10.5-11.5) plus
# 1% for the 300-point grid interpolation.
stopifnot(all(abs(ec90$simulated_ng_ml - ec90$published_ng_ml) <=
  0.5 + 0.01 * ec90$published_ng_ml))
```

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# Ranges: IC50 and m sampled per draw (Table 2 legend), 200 draws per
# concentration on a coarser grid.
conc_coarse <- 10^seq(-4, log10(25), length.out = 40)
phi_var <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = conc_events(conc_coarse, n_rep = 200L),
  params = no_clearance,
  keep = "conc",
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(time == 1) |>
  select(conc, phi_wt, phi_y181c, phi_k103n, phi_g190s) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc, names_to = "strain", values_to = "phi") |>
  group_by(conc, strain) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(phi, 0.025), hi = quantile(phi, 0.975), mean = mean(phi), .groups = "drop")

strain_labels <- c(phi_wt = "wild type", phi_y181c = "Y181C", phi_k103n = "K103N", phi_g190s = "G190S")
ggplot(phi_var, aes(conc, colour = strain, fill = strain)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.30, xmax = 6.55, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "lightyellow") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.35, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * lo, ymax = 100 * hi), alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = 100 * mean)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = strain_labels) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = strain_labels) +
  labs(
    x = "EFV plasma concentration (mg/L)", y = "Prophylactic efficacy (%)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2A of Duwal 2019. Yellow: published 95% range of",
      "400 mg steady-state troughs; dashed: published median."
    )
  )
```

The typical-value curve gives 11.5 ng/mL for wild type, which the paper
rounds to 11; the three mutants agree to within 1%. At the published median
400 mg trough (1.35 mg/L) the model gives complete protection against
wild-type and Y181C virus and about 91% (K103N) and 89% (G190S) against the
two highly resistant mutants -- the paper's "about 90% protection".

```{r figure-2b, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
phi_typ |>
  transmute(
    conc,
    Y181C = phi_wt - phi_y181c,
    K103N = phi_wt - phi_k103n,
    G190S = phi_wt - phi_g190s
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc, names_to = "strain", values_to = "rel") |>
  ggplot(aes(conc, 100 * rel, colour = strain)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.35, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "EFV plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    y = "Relative transmissibility, phi_wt - phi_mut (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the typical-value curves of Figure 2B of Duwal 2019."
  )

at_median <- phi_typ[which.min(abs(phi_typ$conc - 1.35)), ]
stopifnot(
  at_median$phi_wt > 0.99, at_median$phi_y181c > 0.99,
  at_median$phi_wt - at_median$phi_k103n < 0.2,
  at_median$phi_wt - at_median$phi_g190s < 0.2
)
```

# Viral dynamics after exposure during PrEP

The viral states hold the expected numbers of free virions and of early and
productively infected T cells. Without drug, one virion's expected progeny
grows (each virion infects with probability about 0.2, and an integrated cell
releases 670 virions per day), so the mean-field trajectory expands; under
EFV the infection propensity is suppressed and the expected inoculum decays.
This mean trajectory is not the infection probability -- that is `phi`, or the
stochastic simulation of the paper -- but it shows the drug acting where the
model says it acts. Below, a typical subject starts 400 mg daily and is
exposed to one virion of each strain on day 31; a second run has no drug.

```{r viral-dynamics, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
expo <- 30 * 24
vd_events <- function(with_drug) {
  ev <- tibble(id = 1L, time = expo, amt = 1, evid = 1L,
    cmt = c("virus", "virus_y181c", "virus_k103n", "virus_g190s"))
  if (with_drug) {
    ev <- bind_rows(ev, tibble(id = 1L, time = 24 * (0:44), amt = 400, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"))
  }
  bind_rows(ev, tibble(id = 1L, time = seq(expo, expo + 14 * 24, by = 2), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")) |>
    mutate(
      WT = 70, SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = 0L, SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT = 0L,
      SNP_CYP2A6_RS8192726 = 0L, SNP_CYP2A6_RS28399454 = 0L, CYP2B6_MISSING = 0L, OCC = 1L
    ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}
vd <- bind_rows(
  muffle_known(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = vd_events(TRUE), returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(regimen = "EFV 400 mg daily"),
  muffle_known(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = vd_events(FALSE), returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(regimen = "no drug")
) |>
  select(regimen, time, virus, virus_y181c, virus_k103n, virus_g190s) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("virus"), names_to = "strain", values_to = "virions")

ggplot(vd, aes((time - expo) / 24, pmax(virions, 1e-6), colour = strain)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c(virus = "wild type", virus_y181c = "Y181C",
    virus_k103n = "K103N", virus_g190s = "G190S")) +
  labs(x = "Days after exposure", y = "Expected free virions", colour = NULL)

v_end <- vd |> filter(time == max(time))
stopifnot(
  all(v_end$virions[v_end$regimen == "no drug"] > 1),
  v_end$virions[v_end$regimen == "EFV 400 mg daily" & v_end$strain == "virus"] < 1e-3
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Prophylactic efficacy formula.** The paper computes Figure 2A with the
  analytical solution of an earlier publication (Duwal 2018, Eqs. 19-21) and
  does not reprint it. The packaged `phi_*` outputs are the extinction
  probability of the branching process defined by the paper's own reactions
  (6)-(11) with the drug effect held constant. They reproduce the paper's four
  90%-protective concentrations (11, 36, 1287, 1486 ng/mL) to the paper's
  printed precision, so the maintainers take the form to be the one the paper
  used.
- **Not reproduced.** The hybrid stochastic EXTRANDE simulations behind
  Figures 3-4 (exposure model of Eq. 12, adherence sampling, PrEP on demand,
  PEP) are a simulation protocol, not model structure, and are not run here.
- **Viral states as expected values.** Because uninfected T cells are held
  constant, the reactions are linear in the viral states and the ODEs give the
  exact expected numbers. They do not give infection probabilities.
- **Autoinduction parameter.** `cl_time_fdef` is `1 - 5.76/9.86` (alpha =
  0.5842), the paper's own definition of alpha, rather than the rounded 0.58
  of Table 1; with it the simulated day-1 / steady-state half-life ratio
  matches the paper's reported half-lives (35.57 h and 20.77 h) exactly.
- **Autoinduction clock.** Eq. (4) runs from the first EFV dose; the model
  uses `tafd(depot)`, so an event table must start EFV with a dose into
  `depot`.
- **Genotype combinations without an estimate.** Supplementary Table 2 lists
  15 genotype combinations plus missing genotype. Subjects with 516TT and a
  983 C allele, or 516GT with a 983 C allele and both CYP2A6 variants, have no
  estimate; the model returns `NA` clearance for them rather than borrowing
  another group's value. The virtual cohort redraws them (0.7% of draws).
- **Genotype frequencies.** Dickinson 2015 reports only the marginal
  frequency of each SNP, so the cohort draws the four positions independently.
  The resulting clearance distribution matches the paper's Supplementary
  Table 1 closely (table above).
- **IOV in the virtual cohort.** The spread of CLss/F in Supplementary Table 1
  matches the model with both IIV and one draw of IOV, so the cohort uses
  `OCC = 1` throughout.
- **PD variability.** IC50 (log-normal) and m (normal) are sampled per
  simulated subject with the wild-type coefficient of variation, as the
  Table 2 legend states. One eta of each scales all four strains, so within a
  subject the strains' potencies are perfectly correlated; the paper sampled
  each strain separately. Marginal distributions per strain are unaffected.
- **Trial size.** Duwal 2019 Section 2 assigns 311 patients to 600 mg and 295
  to 400 mg, whereas Dickinson 2015 Table 1 has the reverse; the PK model does
  not depend on it.
- **Fraction exceeding 10 mg/L (known deviation).** The paper does not say
  over what time window "eventually exceed" is evaluated; the 30-day window
  here is the span of Figure 1C-D. The paper's 11.3% / 2.5% are not
  reproduced even from its own virtual patients (6.8% / 1.3%), so this
  comparison is reported but not checked.
- **Half-lives and clearance against Supplementary Table 1.** The comparison
  table uses the simulated 400-subject cohort, so its medians carry a few
  percent of sampling error. Run through the model, the paper's own
  Supplementary Table 1 patients give median half-lives of 35.56 h and
  20.77 h, against the published 35.57 h and 20.77 h.
- No correction notice for the article was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-25.
